PullRequest.Title: chat: support selective customization lockdown
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8826

Dependency microsoft/vscode-policy-watcher#75 is merged and `@vscode/policy-watcher@1.5.0` is published.

## Summary

Adds the canonical selective form of `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` while preserving existing boolean behavior:

- `true` continues to block standalone skills, agents, hooks, instructions, and MCP servers.
- arrays containing `skills`, `agents`, `hooks`, and/or `mcp` block only those standalone surfaces.
- plugin-provided customizations remain eligible.
- malformed or partially unknown arrays fail closed instead of applying a weaker partial policy.
- selective arrays intentionally do not map to VS Code instructions; boolean `true` remains the instruction lockdown.

## Implementation

- carries boolean or selective values through server, file, and native managed-settings projection
- keeps the named VS Code policy boolean-only for existing administrative templates
- uses the scalar-union managed-setting API from policy-watcher 1.5.0
- remains compatible with watcher 1.4 by retrying only the first declared scalar type (`boolean`) when the legacy addon rejects a union
- reuses prompt discovery gates for skills, agents, hooks, and embedded agent hooks
- applies MCP selection at registry lookup/start and live-server policy boundaries
- preserves managed-hook, managed-MCP allowlist, strict-marketplace, and plugin provenance behavior
- documents selective semantics, rollout compatibility, and control composition

## Review fixes

Addressed all automated review findings:

- model scalar unions as non-empty tuples
- make native watcher replacement transactional so failed replacement preserves the active watcher
- reject same-ID MCP collection/definition swaps during async connection resolution

## Validation

- merged current `main` and resolved managed-settings changes from upstream
- `npm run export-policy-data` (clean generated policy result; named policy remains boolean)
- 271 targeted policy, account, prompt, hook, and MCP unit tests
- 14 native managed-settings service tests, including legacy fallback and failed replacement
- published policy-watcher 1.5.0 installed and built locally
- policy-watcher Linux, macOS, and Windows Azure builds

Local `typecheck-client` after merging main is blocked by unavailable private SDK packages in this checkout; the pre-merge typecheck passed, and the fresh PR Compile & Hygiene job is the authoritative post-merge validation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop startup and policy-definition updates recreate the native managed-settings watcher
Scenarios.CriticalPath: PolicyConfiguration submits changed policy definitions through AccountPolicyService and the browser-to-main channel; initial desktop policy resolution waits for the main-process native watcher to deliver its initial snapshot. Later account/configuration events await the same path before policy values are recomputed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the policy-definition map from the workbench process to the main-process native managed-settings service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per AccountPolicyService reevaluation that has managed-setting definitions; unchanged definition sets are recognized in the main-process service and reuse initialization. This call frequency predates the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPC update and payload traversal occurred; the diff only permits scalar-union type metadata in the existing payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial configuration/policy resolution awaits the response; later policy refreshes await it before publishing updated values.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create an OS registry/managed-preferences watcher and replace the previous native watcher.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One active watcher; Throttler serializes and coalesces a burst to the active update plus the latest queued update. On a legacy 1.4 addon rejecting scalar unions, the new compatibility path makes one failed synchronous construction attempt followed by one fallback construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A watcher was already created/replaced for each distinct submitted definition set. The diff changes replacement ordering and adds a bounded legacy fallback, without increasing normal-path watcher cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial callback resolves watcher initialization, so startup waits for it. Normal 1.5 operation still constructs one watcher; the legacy retry is constant and only follows immediate type rejection.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of declared managed-setting policies and bursts of policy-definition changes during startup; Throttler reduces concurrent updates to at most one active and one latest queued factory.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Watcher creation is serialized by Throttler. MutableDisposable disposes the previous watcher when a successfully created replacement is installed; failed replacement leaves the old watcher active.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Equal definition maps return the existing initialization path and avoid native watcher recreation. Cold startup dynamically imports the addon and creates the watcher; warm unchanged updates reuse it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the IPC call, equality guard, throttler behavior, replacement disposal, and conditional retry are explicit in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native addon initialization cost is platform-dependent, and legacy-addon fallback prevalence is unknown, but the added work is bounded to one immediate failed attempt in that compatibility case.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The normal path does not add watcher or IPC fan-out, queued replacements are coalesced, and successful replacement keeps exactly one live native watcher.

Scenarios.Scenario: Server- and file-delivered managed settings normalize a selective customization array
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A managed-settings server refresh waits for the existing HTTP response and JSON decoding before policy data is published; a managed-settings file refresh waits for the existing throttled file read. The diff then validates at most four selectors and serializes the array into the existing scalar bag.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET the enterprise managed_settings endpoint and decode its JSON response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per existing managed-settings refresh attempt, with existing request/backoff behavior; the diff does not add requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The endpoint was already fetched and normalized; the diff accepts one additional response shape.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Policy freshness waits for the request and adaptation, but the new selector validation is bounded CPU work after the response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse managed-settings.json after a watched-file event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per refresh, coalesced by a 500 ms ThrottledDelayer; the diff does not add reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same watched file was read and normalized. The diff adds one bounded selector validation/JSON stringify operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: File-policy publication waits for the read and normalization.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Top-level managed-setting key count; the selective selector array is schema-bounded to four recognized strings.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: File changes are delayed/coalesced; server refresh behavior is unchanged. Normalization itself is synchronous and runs once per delivered payload.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache. Existing server freshness/backoff and file-change coalescing remain intact; canonical JSON is produced once per payload and parsed during policy evaluation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all changed normalization operations and their network/file callers were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Payload sizes vary, but the new array is bounded and adds no boundary calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added cloning, validation, stringify, and parse work is bounded and occurs only on existing policy refresh paths.

Scenarios.Scenario: Prompt, skill, agent, and hook discovery reacts to selective lockdown
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Chat consumers request cached discovery results. On a relevant configuration change the existing caches are invalidated; recomputation checks the lockdown before standalone source-folder lookup and filesystem discovery, while plugin contributions remain in their existing observable paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve workspace/user source folders, watch prompt locations, enumerate files, and read prompt metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing discovery scales with workspace roots and discovered prompt files. A selected surface returns before standalone filesystem discovery; an unselected surface performs the same discovery as before plus checks an array of at most four selectors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Boolean true already short-circuited all standalone discovery and false performed it. Selective arrays now choose which surfaces take either existing branch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery consumers await filesystem enumeration on cache misses; selective blocking removes that work for blocked surfaces.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Workspace-root count and prompt/skill/agent/hook file count after existing cache invalidation; selector evaluation is constant-bounded independently of those counts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing CachedPromise instances coalesce discovery per surface; filesystem searches inside discovery retain their existing Promise.all behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold or invalidated caches recompute. Warm consumers reuse CachedPromise results. Policy changes already invalidated the affected caches; the diff does not add a new event source.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the gates run before standalone source-folder/file discovery and cache invalidation wiring was inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Workspace file counts vary, but selected lockdown paths reduce rather than increase I/O and unselected paths add only bounded checks.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed mechanism either preserves existing discovery or short-circuits expensive filesystem work.

Scenarios.Scenario: MCP collection discovery, autostart, manual start, and live policy changes under selective MCP lockdown
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Registry collection filtering runs before lazy discovery and server collection. Starting a server is serialized per server, may activate extensions, read stored inputs, resolve variables, apply sandboxing, then create and start a subprocess or network connection. The diff adds policy/identity checks before connection construction and after asynchronous launch resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate lazy MCP providers/extensions and autostart eligible servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Lazy activation is once per uncached allowed collection. Autostart still fans out with Promise.all across the existing eligible server set; selective MCP blocking removes standalone collections before candidates are formed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Boolean lockdown already filtered all standalone MCP collections. Selective arrays reuse that filtering only when 'mcp' is selected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Collection activation precedes autostart; the diff filters blocked collections before activation and therefore cannot add activation fan-out.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/write persisted MCP input and secret values while resolving a launch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per server connection resolution, subject to existing lazy storage and resolved-input behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same input storage work occurred for every connection resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Connection creation waits for input retrieval and persistence. The new post-resolution checks run after this existing work but add no storage operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch a local MCP server process when the resolved launch is command-based.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One launch per eligible server start/restart, serialized by that server's connection sequencer; existing autostart may start eligible servers concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Eligible servers already launched through the same connection start. The diff adds rejection paths before launch rather than adding launches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Tools become live only after connection start. New policy and collection-identity checks occur before this boundary and can prevent a stale or newly blocked launch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Connect to a remote HTTP/SSE MCP server when the resolved launch is remote.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One connection per eligible server start/restart with the same existing per-server serialization and cross-server autostart concurrency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same remote connection path and cardinality existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remote tools depend on connection establishment; added checks precede and can suppress this boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered collections and distinct server definitions after policy filtering. Added selector scans are bounded to four values; the added final collection lookup is linear in registered collections once per connection resolution.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-server start is sequenced. Existing autostart uses Promise.all across eligible servers. Collection reconciliation is delayed 500 ms, and policy filtering can reduce the eligible set.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Lazy collections skip activation when cached; server metadata caches are unchanged. Selective filtering is reactive and does not defeat those caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: collection filtering, lazy activation, 500 ms reconciliation, per-server sequencing, autostart fan-out, and subprocess/network placement were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installations vary in MCP collection/server count and remote startup latency, but the only newly added per-start work is bounded in-memory validation and one collection lookup.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new checks do not add expensive boundaries or concurrency and prevent stale/blocked servers from reaching process/network startup.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all 21 changed files and all diff pages. Traced policy transport/watcher lifecycle, managed-settings normalization, prompt discovery caches and filesystem work, and MCP discovery/start/live-policy paths. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression was found; no findings or regression-fix records were submitted.
